questiontext.text:
A function \( f : \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}\) is defined by the rule \[ f(x) = {@f1@}. \]

Which input of the function \(f\) has the output \({@output@}\)?

\(x = \) [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]

generalfeedback.text:
To find the input that gives a known output, set the rule equal to the output and solve for \(x\): \[ {@f1@} = {@output@}. \]

[[if test="is(n1<0)"]]

The output is less than 1, so the index must be negative. Since \({@b@}^{ {@negn1@} } = {@ev(b^negn1)@}\), the rule for a negative index gives \({@b@}^{ {@n1@} } = \dfrac{1}{ {@b@}^{ {@negn1@} } } = {@output@}\). Hence \(x = {@n1@}\).

[[else]]

Write the output as a power of the base: \({@output@} = {@b@}^{ {@n1@} }\). Hence \(x = {@n1@}\).

[[/if]]

The answer is unique because an exponential function \(b^x\) with \(b > 1\) is always increasing, so each output comes from exactly one input. The graph shows the horizontal line \(y = {@output@}\) meeting the curve once, at \(x = {@n1@}\).

[[jsxgraph width="320px" height="260px"]] (function() { var base = {#b#}, n = {#n1#}; var out = Math.pow(base, n); var ym = (n > 0) ? 1.25*out : 1.25; var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox: [-4.5, ym, 4.5, -ym/8], axis: true, grid: false, showNavigation: false, showCopyright: false }); board.create('functiongraph', [function(x){ return Math.pow(base, x); }, -4.5, 4.5], {strokeColor: '#1565c0', strokeWidth: 2, fixed: true}); board.create('line', [[0, out], [1, out]], {strokeColor: '#c62828', dash: 2, strokeWidth: 1, fixed: true}); var lab = (n < 0) ? ('(' + n + ', 1/' + Math.pow(base, -n) + ')') : ('(' + n + ', ' + out + ')'); board.create('point', [n, out], {name: lab, size: 3, color: '#c62828', fixed: true, label: {offset: [-8, 14], anchorX: 'right'}}); })(); [[/jsxgraph]]

questiondescription.text: Grade 11 Functions (function notation: finding the input for a given output; overlaps with 16.2 Function Notation). Solves b^x = output for an integer x, positive or negative.

node.description: Diagnostic: sign of the index wrong

truefeedback.text: Check the sign of your input. With your answer, \(f\) gives \({@ev(b^ans1,simp)@}\), not \({@output@}\). For \(b > 1\), a positive index gives an output greater than 1, and a negative index gives a fraction between 0 and 1, because \(b^{-n} = \dfrac{1}{b^n}\).

falsefeedback.text: The value of the function for your input is \({@ev(b^ans1,simp)@}\), which is not equal to \({@output@}\). Try writing \({@output@}\) as a power of \({@b@}\).
